# Fixture lines shaped like `tcpdump -i eth2 -l -n -e arp` output.
# Two dialects are covered on purpose:
#   modern tcpdump (libpcap >= 1.10): "Request who-has X tell Y, length 28"
#                                     "Reply X is-at M, length 28"
#   older tcpdump 4.9.x wording:      "ARP, Request who-has X tell Y, length 28"
#                                     "ARP, Reply X is-at M, length 28"
# On OpenWrt (tcpdump + libpcap from the same feed) the modern form applies,
# but keeping both here pins the parser against the known variants.
#
# Hosts used below:
#   10.10.10.10 / 02:00:00:00:00:0a   (client, requester + replier roles)
#   10.10.10.11 / 02:00:00:00:00:0b   (second client)
#   10.10.10.13 / 02:00:00:00:00:0d   (client whose IP later moves to the
#                                       device with :0e -- MAC-change pin)
#   10.10.10.1  / 02:00:00:00:00:01   (gateway: Router2's LAN side; its
#                                       is-at replies must NOT be learned)
#   192.168.178.1 / 02:00:00:00:00:f0  (FritzBox, default 192.168.178.0/24;
#                                       appears only in garbage lines)

02:00:00:00:00:0a > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: Request who-has 10.10.10.1 tell 10.10.10.10, length 28
02:00:00:00:00:01 > 02:00:00:00:00:0a, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: Reply 10.10.10.1 is-at 02:00:00:00:00:01, length 28
02:00:00:00:00:0a > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: ARP, Request who-has 10.10.10.10 tell 10.10.10.10, length 28
02:00:00:00:00:0b > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: Request who-has 10.10.10.10 tell 10.10.10.11, length 28
02:00:00:00:00:0a > 02:00:00:00:00:0b, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: Reply 10.10.10.10 is-at 02:00:00:00:00:0a, length 28
02:00:00:00:00:0b > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: ARP, Request who-has 10.10.10.1 tell 10.10.10.11, length 28
02:00:00:00:00:01 > 02:00:00:00:00:0b, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: ARP, Reply 10.10.10.1 is-at 02:00:00:00:00:01, length 28
# ---- lines that must NOT produce any host update ----
02:00:00:00:00:0a > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: Request who-has 10.10.10.1 (ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff) tell 10.10.10.10, length 28
02:00:00:00:00:f0 > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype IPv4 (0x0800), length 74: 192.168.178.1.53 > 10.10.10.10.53: 12345 1/0/0 PTR something
listening on eth2, link-type EN10MB (Ethernet), snapshot length 262144 bytes

# ---- LIVE dialect: tcpdump's real output prepends a timestamp ----------
# The parser must treat the MAC as the first MAC-shaped field, not field 1
# (which would be the timestamp). This exact shape is taken from production
# output; it pins the request path against the bug that silently killed it.
16:51:33.077449 02:00:00:00:00:0c > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 60: Request who-has 10.10.10.1 tell 10.10.10.12, length 46
16:51:33.077800 02:00:00:00:00:01 > 02:00:00:00:00:0c, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 60: Reply 10.10.10.1 is-at 02:00:00:00:00:01, length 46
# A KNOWN client answering the gateway's unicast probe (self-announce shape,
# MAC already bound): must refresh the existing binding, NOT re-provision it
# and NOT create anything new. An UNKNOWN self-announce (the gateway's own
# gratuitous lines above) still teaches nothing.
16:52:01.000000 02:00:00:00:00:0a > 02:00:00:00:00:01, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 60: Reply 10.10.10.10 is-at 02:00:00:00:00:0a, length 46
# An ARP probe (ACD/DAD, e.g. a client verifying an address before DHCP):
# the sender field is the unspecified address -- it must NEVER yield a
# binding. This exact shape produced a stray 0.0.0.0 entry on production.
17:11:04.000000 02:00:00:00:00:0a > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 60: Request who-has 10.10.10.1 tell 0.0.0.0, length 46

# ---- MAC CHANGE: an IP moves to a different device ---------------------
# 10.10.10.13 is first learned from :0d; the IP then belongs to the device
# with :0e. The binding must flip to the new MAC (state, map element and
# arpreply rule all re-provision for :0e). Pins the POSIX-sh clobber bug:
# remove_host_rules' `mac="$2"` destroyed update_host's new-MAC value
# before it was written, so the binding could never change and instead
# flapped deprovision/provision with the OLD mac on every ARP (observed
# live on production as 586 flaps on one reused DHCP address).
17:12:00.000000 02:00:00:00:00:0d > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 60: Request who-has 10.10.10.1 tell 10.10.10.13, length 46
17:12:10.000000 02:00:00:00:00:0e > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 60: Request who-has 10.10.10.1 tell 10.10.10.13, length 46
